llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed, read-only VMware Log Insight integration, with expected local configuration, credential use, and audit logging.

dimensions.detail: The skill can read centralized operational logs and authenticate to a configured Log Insight appliance, which is sensitive but expected for this purpose and documented as read-only.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses the uv package vmware-log-insight and local config files under ~/.vmware-log-insight; this is disclosed and coherent with a CLI/MCP integration.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime guidance scopes use to VMware/vSphere/ESXi log investigation, tells agents to bound searches, treat log text as untrusted data, and route unrelated VMware event or metric work to companion skills.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It uses local config, a .env credential file, and an audit database at ~/.vmware/audit.db; these are disclosed local state/audit files, not hidden background persistence or privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is searching and aggregating VMware Aria Operations for Logs data, and the documented tools are consistently described as read-only log, metadata, and alert-history queries with no ingest or alert mutation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let the agent query your VMware Log Insight appliance. Use a least-privilege read-only service account, keep ~/.vmware-log-insight/.env protected, prefer a real secret manager over base64 obfuscation, and leave TLS verification enabled except for controlled lab appliances.
llm.findings:
[SQP-3] unexpected: The non-English phrase in setup documentation is not needed for the skill purpose, but it is a minor wording issue with no security-relevant behavior.
[PE2] expected: The cited chmod 600 examples set restrictive permissions on a credential file; they do not invoke sudo or request root privileges.
[PE3] expected: The .env credential reference is expected for authenticating to the user's configured Log Insight appliance and is disclosed, with guidance to use a secret manager for stronger at-rest secrecy.
[RA2] expected: The cited config files and audit database are disclosed local configuration/audit state for the integration, not cron, startup execution, or unauthorized session persistence.
